## Another September Night, Another Winning Record

You know what 12-3 reminds me of? Those late-season runs where everything just clicks. The rotation's dealing, the bats are alive, and suddenly you remember why you fell in love with this game in the first place. That's what our model did last night—80% accuracy across fifteen matchups. I've been covering baseball long enough to know that kind of hit rate doesn't come around every day.

## The Hits That Landed

The Tigers took care of business against Colorado—again. I'll get to that rematch in a minute, but this is becoming a pattern. Toronto flipped the script on Baltimore, the Rays handled Houston's firepower, and San Diego's bats showed up in San Francisco. These weren't coin flips. These were reads based on matchups, momentum, and the kind of September baseball that separates contenders from pretenders.

## The Two That Got Away

The Yankees couldn't handle the Mets in the Subway Series—sometimes October baseball starts early in New York, and the script gets thrown out. And Miami? Well, the Marlins playing spoiler against the Dodgers is about as classic as it gets. I've seen enough September baseball to know that even 60% confidence picks can go sideways when pride's on the line.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Detroit's Got Another Date

Here's where it gets interesting. Colorado and Detroit run it back on September 13th, and we're even more confident this time around. Jackson Jobe gets the ball for the Tigers at home, and if you've been paying attention, you know what that means. Gabriel Hughes will toe the rubber for the Rockies, and historically—well, let's just say the altitude advantage doesn't travel well to Comerica Park.

## The Veteran's Take

Sixty-nine percent confidence isn't just a number—it's a reflection of what we saw last night and what the matchup data is screaming. Jobe's been solid at home, the Tigers' lineup has found its rhythm, and Colorado's road woes are well-documented. I've covered enough rematches to know this: when a team wins convincingly once, they usually have the mental edge the second time around.

See you tomorrow when we break down how it all played out. Same time, same game, different results—or so we hope.
